result.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Urdu Nastaliq Handwriting Recognition
result.summary: Handwritten Urdu is hard to recognize because the cursive Nastaliq script has no fixed baseline and no clear character boundaries. We benchmark six systems on the Urdu Nastaliq Handwritten Dataset (UNHD): Tesseract (default configuration), a script-specific recognizer trained on printed Urdu (UTRNet-Large), two open-source vision-language models (VLMs), and two commercial VLMs. All six systems are evaluated without fine-tuning on 2,465 single-line images (Part A), and the four VLMs receive the same fixed prompt (decoding uses temperature 0 where configurable, except for Claude Sonnet 5, whose decoding cannot be configured). Both commercial VLMs reach lower error than the printed-Urdu recognizer and the open-source VLMs. We do not compare against handwriting-trained recognizers, which would likely do better in-domain; we characterize zero-shot behavior, not state of the art. We also describe three distinct failure modes among the ranked systems. In one of them, a commercial model explicitly declines to transcribe a few very hard-to-read images instead of guessing. In a second study (Part B), VLMs correct the output of a separate OCR system using both the source image and the noisy text. Once separated from each model's own reading ability, the benefit is small on Tesseract's output (0.7% to 7.4%) and larger (17.9% and 21.9%) only for the two commercial correctors given UTRNet's text. It appears to depend on how legible the supplied text already is, and a weaker corrector can make a more legible text worse.

AI.brief_summary: 在 UNHD 乌尔都语 Nastaliq 手写单行图像上零样本评测六种系统（Tesseract、印刷体识别器、两个开源与两个商用 VLM），并另设实验让 VLM 结合原图与含噪 OCR 文本做纠错，分析增益大小与三类失效模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线联系较弱，主要是识别准确率评测；但 Part B 试图把模型自身识读能力与「依据原图修正给定文本」的贡献分开，可供核查 VLM 是否真以视觉证据覆盖文本先验，以及较弱纠正器反而使较清晰文本变差的现象。
